A short guide What is pain? And why it can hang around after the injury has healed.
Pain is an alarm Your brain makes pain to protect you . It is always real. It is not ‘in your head’ in the made-up sense.
Most of the time The alarm works brilliantly. Step on a pin → ouch → you move your foot. Job done, alarm off.
quiet LOUD But sometimes The alarm gets too sensitive . After months of pain the nervous system can turn the volume up. Doctors call this sensitisation .
Hurt ≠ harm Like a smoke alarm going off for burnt toast . Loud alarm, little danger. In chronic pain, hurting often doesn’t mean you’re doing damage.
quiet LOUD Things that turn it up Pain volume up ↑ Poor sleep Stress & worry Not moving Low mood Fear of moving
quiet LOUD Things that turn it down Pain volume down ↓ Gentle movement Pacing Good sleep Understanding pain People Therapies
You can retrain the alarm Small steps, most days. Flares happen. They’re a bump, not a fall back to the start.
